cases.title: Loopback-only network use is allowed; non-loopback outbound connections stay at 0
cases.rationale: PROPOSED. The blueprint (section on Kedro hooks and datasets, architecture line 282) forbids network and Kedro telemetry but does not name a loopback exception. The case proposes that 127.0.0.1, ::1 and localhost are allowed and that every other address counts.

cases.title: Observable for N13: recording guards on socket.create_connection and socket.getaddrinfo

expected.guard_behavior: append the call arguments to a list; for a loopback address (127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost) call the original function and return its result; for any other address raise OSError so that no packet leaves the host
expected.outbound_connections_means: recorded create_connection and connect calls whose address is not 127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost
expected.dns_lookups_to_non_loopback_means: recorded getaddrinfo calls whose host is not 127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost
expected.guard_self_check: before the run, one getaddrinfo call to a name under example.invalid must be recorded exactly once, then the list is cleared
expected.known_limit: the observer sees Python-level calls only; a subprocess or a C extension that opens its own socket is outside it, and so are socket.socket.connect_ex, UDP sendto, and names bound before the guard is installed (for example from socket import getaddrinfo)

cases.rationale: PROPOSED. T0-10-N13 states counts of 0 but not how a test sees them. The execution plan (F0-04) asks for socket and real-network deny controls but names no observable. This case fixes one observable so that a consuming test cannot pass because the guard was never installed.

cases.provenance: TASK-GOAL DECISION (T0-10 security and privacy). A1 text for A1 logging: docs/microsoft-graph-error-handling.md says arbitrary exception text is not printed. The A2 blueprint (architecture line 282) says user content must not enter names or exception text. No A1 text names the Authorization header for A2.
cases.title: An Authorization header or bearer value never reaches a log or a stored error

input.exception_message: 401 Unauthorized for request with Authorization: Bearer FAKE-TOKEN-0000

cases.rationale: FAKE-TOKEN-0000 is an obviously fake canary. The case checks the value only. It does not fix the replacement text.

cases.provenance: TASK-GOAL DECISION (T0-10 security and privacy). A1 text: docs/microsoft-graph-error-handling.md says the Graph diagnostics middleware 'never logs the Graph URL or payload' and that opaque URLs and arbitrary exception text are not printed. The same rule for A2 exceptions is the task goal.
cases.title: A Graph-style URL with a query token inside an exception message is redacted before logging
cases.rationale: FAKE-TOKEN-0001 is an obviously fake canary. The order matters: redaction runs before any log handler sees the text, so a handler that is added later cannot leak it.
